claim: Messenger RNA localization is important for cell motility by local protein translation.
source: Messenger RNA localization is important for cell motility by local protein translation.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a general principle underlying the study.

claim: Single mRNAs can be imaged and their movements tracked in single cells.
source: However, while single mRNAs can be imaged and their movements tracked in single cells, it has not yet been possible to determine whether these mRNAs are actively translating.
evidence: This is stated as established capability in the abstract.

claim: It has not been possible to determine whether single tracked mRNAs are actively translating.
source: However, while single mRNAs can be imaged and their movements tracked in single cells, it has not yet been possible to determine whether these mRNAs are actively translating.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation in the abstract that the current work addresses.

claim: Single β-actin mRNAs were imaged tagged with MS2 stem loops colocalizing with labeled ribosomes to determine when polysomes formed.
source: Therefore, we imaged single β-actin mRNAs tagged with MS2 stem loops colocalizing with labeled ribosomes to determine when polysomes formed.
evidence: This describes the experimental approach used in the study.

claim: mRNAs co-moving with ribosomes have significantly different diffusion properties from non-translating mRNAs that were exposed to translation inhibitors.
source: A dataset of tracking information consisting of thousands of trajectories per cell demonstrated that mRNAs co-moving with ribosomes have significantly different diffusion properties from non-translating mRNAs that were exposed to translation inhibitors.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figures 2 and 4.

claim: Ribosome load changes mRNA movement.
source: These data indicate that ribosome load changes mRNA movement and therefore highly translating mRNAs move slower.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data presented in the abstract.

claim: Highly translating mRNAs move slower.
source: These data indicate that ribosome load changes mRNA movement and therefore highly translating mRNAs move slower.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion stated in the abstract and supported by data throughout the manuscript.

claim: β-actin mRNA near focal adhesions exhibited sub-diffusive corralled movement characteristic of increased translation.
source: Importantly, β-actin mRNA near focal adhesions exhibited sub-diffusive corralled movement characteristic of increased translation.
evidence: This is a key finding stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figures 1 and 4.

claim: This method can identify where ribosomes become engaged for local protein production.
source: This method can identify where ribosomes become engaged for local protein production and how spatial regulation of mRNA-protein interactions mediates cell directionality.
evidence: This is stated as a capability of the method in the abstract.

claim: Spatial regulation of mRNA-protein interactions mediates cell directionality.
source: This method can identify where ribosomes become engaged for local protein production and how spatial regulation of mRNA-protein interactions mediates cell directionality.
evidence: This is stated as a capability of the method in the abstract.

claim: mRNA compartmentalization is a conserved mechanism cells use to spatially control protein translation through zipcode sequences often in the transcript's 3'UTR.
source: mRNA compartmentalization is a conserved mechanism cells use to spatially control protein translation through zipcode sequences often in the transcript's 3'UTR (Kislauskis and Singer, 1992; Holt and Bullock, 2009; Pratt and Mowry, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: MS2 binding sites inserted adjacent to the zipcode sequence in the 3'UTR of β-actin mRNA can be used to label and track the movement of single mRNA molecules.
source: Previous work has shown that MS2 binding sites (MBS) inserted adjacent to the zipcode sequence in the 3'UTR of β-actin mRNA can be used to label and track the movement of single mRNA molecules (Fusco et al., 2003; Yamagishi et al., 2009; Lionnet et al., 2011; Katz et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: mRNA exhibited multiple movement profiles (directed, diffusive, and corralled).
source: Previous studies identified that mRNA: (1) exhibited multiple movement profiles (directed, diffusive, and corralled), (2) zipcode sequences facilitated directed transport of β-actin mRNA along microtubules, and (3) zipcode binding protein 1 (ZBP1) delivered β-actin mRNA to leading edge adhesions where it could dwell for more than a minute.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from previous studies.

claim: Zipcode sequences facilitated directed transport of β-actin mRNA along microtubules.
source: Previous studies identified that mRNA: (1) exhibited multiple movement profiles (directed, diffusive, and corralled), (2) zipcode sequences facilitated directed transport of β-actin mRNA along microtubules, and (3) zipcode binding protein 1 (ZBP1) delivered β-actin mRNA to leading edge adhesions where it could dwell for more than a minute.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from previous studies.

claim: Zipcode binding protein 1 (ZBP1) delivered β-actin mRNA to leading edge adhesions where it could dwell for more than a minute.
source: Previous studies identified that mRNA: (1) exhibited multiple movement profiles (directed, diffusive, and corralled), (2) zipcode sequences facilitated directed transport of β-actin mRNA along microtubules, and (3) zipcode binding protein 1 (ZBP1) delivered β-actin mRNA to leading edge adhesions where it could dwell for more than a minute.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from previous studies.

claim: ZBP1 was previously shown to deliver its mRNA target in a translationally silenced state by blocking the 60S ribosomal subunit from initiating translation.
source: ZBP1 was previously shown to deliver its mRNA target in a translationally silenced state by blocking the 60S ribosomal subunit from initiating translation.
evidence: This is stated as previous knowledge.

claim: Once the RNA-protein complex (RNP) localized to the cell periphery, Src kinase phosphorylated the 396 tyrosine to relax translation repression.
source: Once the RNA-protein complex (RNP) localized to the cell periphery, Src kinase phosphorylated the 396 tyrosine to relax translation repression (Hüttelmaier et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Elongation factor 1α (EF1α) may act to anchor mRNA to formins and thereby the leading edge actin cytoskeleton.
source: How translating mRNA can be retained within this compartment is still unclear, although evidence has suggested that the elongation factor 1α (EF1α) may act to anchor mRNA to formins and thereby the leading edge actin cytoskeleton (Liu et al., 2002).
evidence: This is stated as a hypothesis supported by a citation.

claim: The actin cytoskeleton was previously shown to be necessary for mRNA localization and maintenance at the leading edge of migrating fibroblasts.
source: Accordingly, the actin cytoskeleton was previously shown to be necessary for mRNA localization and maintenance at the leading edge of migrating fibroblasts (Sundell and Singer, 1991).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: The RNP size is the main determinant of localization and therefore the architecture of the cytoplasmic microenvironment is a major factor in RNA retention at the leading edge.
source: A recent report also argued that the RNP size is the main determinant of localization and therefore the architecture of the cytoplasmic microenvironment is a major factor in RNA retention at the leading edge (Yamagishi et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated as an argument from a previous report.

claim: Delivery to a local site for increased translation may inherently increase β-actin mRNA dwell times and determine cell polarity and consequent directed motility.
source: Our results suggest that delivery to a local site for increased translation may inherently increase β-actin mRNA dwell times and determine cell polarity and consequent directed motility (Park et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated as a suggestion based on the results of this study and supported by a citation.

claim: MBS bound by the GFP-fused coat proteins (MCP) make single molecule imaging of mRNA technically feasible.
source: MBS bound by the GFP-fused coat proteins (MCP) make single molecule imaging of mRNA technically feasible (Shav-Tal et al., 2004), but it has not been possible to image translation at the single molecule level.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: It has not been possible to image translation at the single molecule level.
source: MBS bound by the GFP-fused coat proteins (MCP) make single molecule imaging of mRNA technically feasible (Shav-Tal et al., 2004), but it has not been possible to image translation at the single molecule level.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation prior to this work.

claim: An approach was developed using binding sites in the coding region that indicated when the first ribosome passed through the mRNA, but this biosensor detected only the pioneer round of translation.
source: Recently, an approach was developed using binding sites in the coding region that indicated when the first ribosome passed through the mRNA, but this biosensor detected only the pioneer round of translation (Halstead et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated as a recent development supported by a citation.

claim: A novel method for tracking ribosomes simultaneously with labeled mRNA resulted in a high-resolution spatial map of mRNAs actively interacting and moving with ribosomes.
source: A novel method for tracking ribosomes simultaneously with labeled mRNA resulted in a high-resolution spatial map of mRNAs actively interacting and moving with ribosomes.
evidence: This is stated as a methodological contribution of the study.

claim: mRNAs that travel with ribosomes were found to move slower and be more spatially confined.
source: mRNAs that travel with ribosomes were likewise found to move slower and be more spatially confined.
evidence: This is stated as a finding in the introduction and supported by data in the results.

claim: When translation inhibitors were used to dissociate ribosomes from mRNA, the average diffusion coefficient of β-actin mRNA increased.
source: When translation inhibitors were used to dissociate ribosomes from mRNA, the average diffusion coefficient of β-actin mRNA increased.
evidence: This is stated as a finding in the introduction and supported by data in Figure 2.

claim: It is possible to map regions of active translation based on movement profiles within a given cellular compartment.
source: Therefore it is possible to map regions of active translation based on movement profiles within a given cellular compartment.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the introduction.

claim: Constitutive expression of tdMCP-GFP labeled all endogenous β-actin mRNA derived from a mouse in which 24 MS2 binding sites (MBS) were inserted into both alleles of the Actb gene.
source: Constitutive expression of tdMCP-GFP labeled all endogenous β-actin mRNA derived from a mouse in which 24 MS2 binding sites (MBS) were inserted into both alleles of the Actb gene (Lionnet et al., 2011).
evidence: This describes the experimental system used, supported by a citation.

claim: Cells were transfected with paxillin-mCherry to label focal adhesions and spatially distinguish the cell's leading edge.
source: Cells were transfected with paxillin-mCherry to label focal adhesions and spatially distinguish the cell's leading edge (Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This describes the experimental approach and references figures showing the results.

claim: Both fast and slow moving mRNAs were tracked with TIRF excitation at a frame time of 35 ms.
source: We tracked both fast and slow moving mRNAs with TIRF excitation at a frame time of 35 ms (Video 1).
evidence: This describes the experimental method and references a video.

claim: mRNA trajectories with lifetimes beyond 105 ms (three consecutive frames) were used to build a β-actin mRNA diffusion map.
source: We used mRNA trajectories with lifetimes beyond 105 ms (three consecutive frames) to build a β-actin mRNA diffusion map, in which all trajectories were given equal weight, regardless of their duration (Figure 1F and 1G, see materials and methods for more details).
evidence: This describes the analysis method and references figures.

claim: Spatially averaged mRNA diffusion maps distinguish cell compartments that channel or restrict mRNA movement.
source: Spatially averaged mRNA diffusion maps distinguish cell compartments that channel or restrict mRNA movement (Figure 1F and Video 2).
evidence: This is stated as a finding and supported by figures and video.

claim: A subset of dwelling mRNAs around focal adhesions represented sites of increased translation.
source: Previous work suggested that a subset of dwelling mRNAs around focal adhesions represented sites of increased translation (Katz et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated as a suggestion from previous work supported by a citation.

claim: Diffusion maps revealed that mRNA movement around adhesions was slower.
source: Diffusion maps revealed that mRNA movement around adhesions was indeed slower (Figure 1B,C, and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated as a finding and supported by figures.

claim: β-actin mRNA at adhesions moved on average 37% slower according to a single-diffusive component fit.
source: A single-diffusive component fit of the cumulative distribution function (CDF) curves determined that β-actin mRNA at adhesions moved on average 37% slower (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A vs. 2B).
evidence: This is stated as a quantitative finding and supported by figures.

claim: The CDF curves are much better fit by a linear combination of two states, a faster one with an apparent diffusion coefficient of 0.4 μm2/s, and a slower one with a coefficient of 0.1 μm2/s.
source: However, the CDF curves are much better fit by a linear combination of two states, a faster one with an apparent diffusion coefficient of 0.4 μm2/s, and a slower one with a coefficient of 0.1 μm2/s (Figure 1B, Figure 1—figure supplement 2C,D).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from data analysis and supported by figures.

claim: Near focal adhesions, the population of fast mRNA species falls from 60% to 50%.
source: Near focal adhesions, the population of fast mRNA species falls from 60% to 50% (Figure 1B), which indicates that around focal adhesions mRNAs diffuse slower and dwell longer on average (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is stated as a quantitative finding and supported by figures.

claim: Around focal adhesions mRNAs diffuse slower and dwell longer on average.
source: Near focal adhesions, the population of fast mRNA species falls from 60% to 50% (Figure 1B), which indicates that around focal adhesions mRNAs diffuse slower and dwell longer on average (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the data and supported by figures.

claim: The mean square displacement (MSD) curves of adhesion-localized mRNAs plateau at a much lower level, demonstrating a significant shift towards a corralled movement profile.
source: Figure 1C depicts the mean square displacement (MSD) curves of adhesion-localized mRNAs, which plateaus at a much lower level. This plateau demonstrates a significant shift towards a corralled movement profile (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is stated as a finding and supported by Figure 1C.

claim: Local confinement of mRNA may indicate that β-actin mRNAs are trapped in areas of localized translation around focal adhesions.
source: This local confinement may indicate that β-actin mRNAs are trapped in areas of localized translation around focal adhesions.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the corralled movement data.

claim: mRNAs would exhibit restricted movement as ribosomes or other RNA binding proteins accumulate on the transcript, thereby increasing its mass and stokes radius.
source: We next hypothesized that mRNAs would exhibit restricted movement as ribosomes or other RNA binding proteins accumulate on the transcript, thereby increasing its mass and stokes radius.
evidence: This is stated as a hypothesis to be tested.

claim: Puromycin and hippuristanol are drugs that disrupt mRNA-ribosome interactions.
source: In order to test this, we dissociated ribosomes from β-actin mRNA with puromycin and hippuristanol, both drugs that disrupt mRNA-ribosome interactions (Joklik and Becker, 1965; Bordeleau et al., 2006; Darnell et al., 2011; Wu et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: After puromycin treatment, β-actin mRNA trajectories showed a significant shift of movement towards the faster diffusing population.
source: After treatment, β-actin mRNA trajectories showed a significant shift of movement towards the faster diffusing population (Videos 3 and 4).
evidence: This is stated as a finding and supported by videos.

claim: After puromycin treatment, ~90% of mRNAs are in the fast population state.
source: The average CDF from five separate acquisitions after puromycin treatment fit well with the linear combination of two CDFs, but now with ~90% of mRNAs being in the fast population state (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated as a quantitative finding and supported by Figure 2A.

claim: The MSD curve and the histogram of average apparent diffusion coefficients displayed a significant shift to faster diffusion after puromycin treatment when compared to steady state β-actin mRNA movement.
source: Likewise, the MSD curve as well as the histogram of average apparent diffusion coefficients also displayed a significant shift to faster diffusion after puromycin treatment when compared to steady state β-actin mRNA movement (Figure 2B and 2C).
evidence: This is stated as a finding and supported by figures.

claim: The translation initiation inhibitor hippuristanol showed the same increase in mRNA diffusion after 1 μM treatment for 20 min.
source: The translation initiation inhibitor hippuristanol showed the same increase in mRNA diffusion after 1 μM treatment for 20 min (Figure 2—figure supplement 1, Video 4).
evidence: This is stated as a finding and supported by a figure and video.

claim: The 60S large subunit protein L10A was labeled with PATagRFP for single particle tracking using photo-activated localization microscopy (sptPALM).
source: To image single ribosomes, the 60S large subunit protein L10A was labeled with PATagRFP for single particle tracking using photo-activated localization microscopy (sptPALM).
evidence: This describes the experimental method used.

claim: Stable expression of fluorescently labeled L10A has been shown to label ~40% of ribosomes.
source: Stable expression of fluorescently labeled L10A has been shown to label ~40% of ribosomes (Wu et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Ribosomes could be tracked for an average lifetime of ~200 ms (6.2 frames) after applying 405 nm activation energy.
source: Ribosomes could be tracked for an average lifetime of ~200 ms (6.2 frames) after applying 405 nm activation energy.
evidence: This describes the experimental observation.

claim: Ribosomes exhibited heterogeneity in diffusive motion, much as with β-actin mRNA.
source: Ribosomes exhibited heterogeneity in diffusive motion, much as with β-actin mRNA (Video 5).
evidence: This is stated as an observation and supported by a video.

claim: Ribosome movement in cells at steady-state is best fit with a two-component fit: with a linear combination of a fast apparent diffusion coefficient of 0.4 μm2/s, and a slower one with a coefficient of 0.1 μm2/s.
source: Ribosome movement in cells at steady-state is best fit with the same two-component fit as mRNA: with a linear combination of a fast apparent diffusion coefficient of 0.4 μm2/s, and a slower one with a coefficient of 0.1 μm2/s.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from data analysis.

claim: Ribosomes collectively show a shift towards a slower diffusion component as compared to β-actin mRNA (56% vs. 42%, respectively).
source: A two-component fit of experimentally obtained CDFs of ribosome trajectories reveals that ribosomes collectively show a shift towards a slower diffusion component as compared to β-actin mRNA (56% vs. 42%, respectively) and suggests most ribosomes actively engage in translation throughout the cytoplasm (compare Figure 2A vs. 2F).
evidence: This is stated as a quantitative finding and supported by figures.

claim: Most ribosomes actively engage in translation throughout the cytoplasm.
source: A two-component fit of experimentally obtained CDFs of ribosome trajectories reveals that ribosomes collectively show a shift towards a slower diffusion component as compared to β-actin mRNA (56% vs. 42%, respectively) and suggests most ribosomes actively engage in translation throughout the cytoplasm (compare Figure 2A vs. 2F).
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the data and supported by figures.

claim: With the addition of puromycin, a significant increase in ribosome diffusion was observed.
source: With the addition of puromycin, a significant increase in ribosome diffusion was observed just as with β-actin mRNA (Figure 2F), and the population of faster ribosomes increased to 73% (Figure 2—figure supplement 2B, Video 6).
evidence: This is stated as a finding and supported by figures and video.

claim: The population of faster ribosomes increased to 73% after puromycin treatment.
source: With the addition of puromycin, a significant increase in ribosome diffusion was observed just as with β-actin mRNA (Figure 2F), and the population of faster ribosomes increased to 73% (Figure 2—figure supplement 2B, Video 6).
evidence: This is stated as a quantitative finding and supported by figures and video.

claim: When β-actin mRNAs are tethered to focal adhesions, ribosomes diffused significantly slower.
source: When β-actin mRNAs are tethered to focal adhesions, ribosomes diffused significantly slower (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated as a finding and supported by a figure.

claim: Tracking of ribosomes in cells with β-actin mRNA tethered to adhesions shifted the movement of ribosomes towards corralled diffusion (63% vs. 56% slow).
source: Tracking of ribosomes in cells with β-actin mRNA tethered to adhesions shifted the movement of ribosomes towards corralled diffusion (63% vs. 56% slow, see Figure 2F,G, Figure 2—figure supplement 2A vs. 2C, Figure 3G and Video 7).
evidence: This is stated as a quantitative finding and supported by figures and video.

claim: Puromycin addition increased the movement of ribosomes in cells with mRNA tethered to adhesions.
source: Puromycin addition increased the movement of ribosomes in cells with mRNA tethered to adhesions (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B and Video 8).
evidence: This is stated as a finding and supported by a figure and video.

claim: sptPALM of ribosomes in the TIRF field can identify ribosomes actively engaged and translating β-actin mRNA.
source: This is also the case for ribosomes in cells with non-tethered cytoplasmic β-actin mRNA (Figure 2F,G, and Video 6 and 9), suggesting that sptPALM of ribosomes in the TIRF field can identify ribosomes actively engaged and translating β-actin mRNA.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the data and supported by figures and videos.

claim: Translating mRNAs should appear as mRNA particles moving while associated with a ribosome.
source: We reasoned that translating mRNAs should appear as mRNA particles moving while associated with a ribosome.
evidence: This is stated as reasoning underlying the experimental approach.

claim: Analyzing co-moving particles should allow characterizing translation compartmentalization in migrating fibroblasts.
source: Analyzing co-moving particles should therefore allow characterizing translation compartmentalization in migrating fibroblasts.
evidence: This is stated as reasoning underlying the experimental approach.

claim: Simultaneous TIRF excitation of GFP labeled β-actin mRNA and PATagRFP labeled ribosomes enabled dual-color single molecule tracking using two synchronized EMCCD cameras.
source: Simultaneous TIRF excitation of GFP labeled β-actin mRNA and PATagRFP labeled ribosomes (fluorescently activated by a 405 nm laser) enabled dual-color single molecule tracking using two synchronized EMCCD cameras (Figure 3A–B).
evidence: This describes the experimental method and references figures.

claim: Only a subset of β-actin mRNA were identified as co-moving with ribosomes.
source: Consistent with this experimental limit, only a subset of β-actin mRNA were identified as co-moving with ribosomes (Figure 3C–D; Figure 4—figure supplement 3A).
evidence: This is stated as an observation and supported by figures.

claim: mRNAs that co-moved with ribosomes were likely loaded with multiple ribosomes and may exhibit slower movement.
source: We hypothesized those mRNAs that co-moved with ribosomes were likely loaded with multiple ribosomes and may exhibit slower movement.
evidence: This is stated as a hypothesis.

claim: Diffusion analysis showed a shift towards slower movement in the co-moving mRNA population.
source: Consistent with this, diffusion analysis showed a shift towards slower movement in the co-moving mRNA population (Figure 3D; Figure 3—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is stated as a finding and supported by figures.

claim: mRNAs found to co-move with ribosomes shifted towards slower and more corralled movement.
source: mRNAs found to co-move with ribosomes shifted towards slower (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A, Figure 4B) and more corralled movement (Figure 3—figure supplement 2B), an indication that these mRNAs were in polysomes and were more likely to dwell locally.
evidence: This is stated as a finding and supported by figures.

claim: mRNAs that co-move with ribosomes were in polysomes and were more likely to dwell locally.
source: mRNAs found to co-move with ribosomes shifted towards slower (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A, Figure 4B) and more corralled movement (Figure 3—figure supplement 2B), an indication that these mRNAs were in polysomes and were more likely to dwell locally.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the data and supported by figures.

claim: Ribosomes found to co-move with β-actin mRNA trended slower and more corralled, reminiscent of mRNA localized to focal adhesions.
source: Likewise, ribosomes found to co-move with β-actin mRNA trended slower and more corralled, reminiscent of mRNA localized to focal adhesions (Figure 2—figure supplement 2E compared to Figure 1C).
evidence: This is stated as a finding and supported by figures.

claim: The analysis of the mobility and co-movement of mRNA and ribosomes provide a detailed picture of the translational landscape inside live cells, capable of identifying translational hotspots.
source: Together, the analysis of the mobility and co-movement of mRNA and ribosomes provide a detailed picture of the translational landscape inside live cells, capable of identifying translational hotspots (Figure 3D,G).
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion and supported by figures.

claim: β-actin mRNA localized to adhesion complexes, presumably synthesizing protein to enhance focal adhesion stabilization and directed migration.
source: Localization of mRNAs has long been proposed to spatially regulate translation, but this has not been directly observed in live cells. In order to address this question, we set out to test previous findings showing that β-actin mRNA localized to adhesion complexes, presumably synthesizing protein to enhance focal adhesion stabilization and directed migration (Katz et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated as a previous finding supported by a citation.

claim: A majority of ribosome-bound mRNA near the focal adhesions diffused slower than ribosome-bound mRNA away from focal adhesions.
source: Consistent with this prediction, a majority of ribosome-bound mRNA near the focal adhesions diffused slower than ribosome-bound mRNA away from focal adhesions (Figure 3—figure supplement 2B), and much slower than mRNA detected without ribosomes, where the two-component fit to the CDF revealed only 34% of slow-moving mRNAs (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is stated as a finding and supported by figures.

claim: mRNA detected without ribosomes near focal adhesions had only 34% of slow-moving mRNAs according to the two-component fit to the CDF.
source: Consistent with this prediction, a majority of ribosome-bound mRNA near the focal adhesions diffused slower than ribosome-bound mRNA away from focal adhesions (Figure 3—figure supplement 2B), and much slower than mRNA detected without ribosomes, where the two-component fit to the CDF revealed only 34% of slow-moving mRNAs (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is stated as a quantitative finding and supported by a figure.

claim: HMM-Bayes fits two diffusive motion states with different diffusion coefficients and automatically annotates the individual steps of each trajectory as corresponding to either the high diffusion state or the low diffusion state.
source: HMM-Bayes fits two diffusive motion states with different diffusion coefficients and automatically annotates the individual steps of each trajectory as corresponding to either the high diffusion state (blue) or the low diffusion state (green) (see Figure 4C to F and Figure 4—figure supplement 1 and 3).
evidence: This describes the analysis method and references figures.

claim: HMM-Bayes automatically annotates stochastic motion dynamics, including the possibility of directed or active transport, without any user-supplied averaging parameters.
source: In contrast to mean-square-displacement analysis that averages heterogeneous motion over predetermined temporal windows within each trajectory, HMM-Bayes automatically annotates stochastic motion dynamics, including the possibility of directed or active transport, without any user-supplied averaging parameters.
evidence: This describes the capabilities of the HMM-Bayes method.

claim: HMM-Bayes can provide insight into switching rates and lifetimes of the fast (D1) and slow (D2) diffusive states.
source: Unlike our trajectory-averaged analysis, HMM-Bayes can provide insight into switching rates and lifetimes of the fast (D1) and slow (D2) diffusive states.
evidence: This describes the capabilities of the HMM-Bayes method.

claim: The slow diffusing state D2 is much longer lived for co-moving ribosomes (1.3 s) as compared to mRNAs that are not observed to be co-moving (0.3 s).
source: It revealed that the slow diffusing state D2 is much longer lived for co-moving ribosomes (1.3 s) as compared to mRNAs that are not observed to be co-moving (0.3 s), consistent with translating ribosomes having a higher propensity to dwell at sites of translation (compare Figure 4—figure supplement 2C with 3C).
evidence: This is stated as a quantitative finding and supported by figures.

claim: Translating ribosomes have a higher propensity to dwell at sites of translation.
source: It revealed that the slow diffusing state D2 is much longer lived for co-moving ribosomes (1.3 s) as compared to mRNAs that are not observed to be co-moving (0.3 s), consistent with translating ribosomes having a higher propensity to dwell at sites of translation (compare Figure 4—figure supplement 2C with 3C).
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the data and supported by figures.

claim: All three species (co-moving ribosomes, co-moving mRNA, and non-co-moving mRNA) have fast diffusing states D1 with similar lifetimes of ~0.5 s.
source: Interestingly, all three species have fast diffusing states D1 with similar lifetimes of ~0.5 s (Figure 4E and Figure 4—figure supplement 2B and 3B), which may suggest that away from sites of active translation all three species explore the cytoplasmic nanoenvironment in similar ways.
evidence: This is stated as a finding and supported by figures.

claim: Away from sites of active translation all three species explore the cytoplasmic nanoenvironment in similar ways.
source: Interestingly, all three species have fast diffusing states D1 with similar lifetimes of ~0.5 s (Figure 4E and Figure 4—figure supplement 2B and 3B), which may suggest that away from sites of active translation all three species explore the cytoplasmic nanoenvironment in similar ways.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the data and supported by figures.

claim: Ribosomes co-localize predominately with the slow diffusive mRNA state close to focal adhesions.
source: As depicted in Figure 4C inset, ribosomes co-localize predominately with the slow diffusive mRNA state (in green) close to focal adhesions, and we hypothesize that the lower diffusion coefficient corresponds to a condition in which the mRNAs are loaded with polysomes within specific nanoenvironments of active translation.
evidence: This is stated as an observation and supported by a figure.

claim: The lower diffusion coefficient corresponds to a condition in which the mRNAs are loaded with polysomes within specific nanoenvironments of active translation.
source: As depicted in Figure 4C inset, ribosomes co-localize predominately with the slow diffusive mRNA state (in green) close to focal adhesions, and we hypothesize that the lower diffusion coefficient corresponds to a condition in which the mRNAs are loaded with polysomes within specific nanoenvironments of active translation.
evidence: This is stated as a hypothesis and supported by a figure.

claim: Given a translation rate of 5.6 amino acids per second, the time to translate one β-actin protein molecule is estimated to be 67 s.
source: Interestingly, lifetimes of the slow state for co-moving ribosomes and mRNAs revealed by the HMM-Bayes are transient in nature and are much shorter than the translation time: given a translation rate of 5.6 amino acids per second (Ingolia et al., 2011) we estimate the time to translate one β-actin protein molecule to be 67 s.
evidence: This is stated as a calculation based on a cited translation rate.

claim: Lifetimes of the slow state for co-moving ribosomes and mRNAs are transient in nature and are much shorter than the translation time.
source: Interestingly, lifetimes of the slow state for co-moving ribosomes and mRNAs revealed by the HMM-Bayes are transient in nature and are much shorter than the translation time: given a translation rate of 5.6 amino acids per second (Ingolia et al., 2011) we estimate the time to translate one β-actin protein molecule to be 67 s.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the HMM-Bayes analysis.

claim: The transient slow state is both more abundant and more stable for co-moving ribosomes at focal adhesions.
source: The transient slow state is both more abundant and more stable for co-moving ribosomes at focal adhesions, which suggests that translating ribosomes have higher propensity to dwell within specific nanoenvironments close to focal adhesions.
evidence: This is stated as a finding.

claim: Translating ribosomes have higher propensity to dwell within specific nanoenvironments close to focal adhesions.
source: The transient slow state is both more abundant and more stable for co-moving ribosomes at focal adhesions, which suggests that translating ribosomes have higher propensity to dwell within specific nanoenvironments close to focal adhesions.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the data.

claim: Local ribosome confinement can be enhanced by artificially tethering β-actin mRNA to focal adhesions.
source: While the microscopic mechanism of transient translational confinement is unknown, this local ribosome confinement can be enhanced by artificially tethering β-actin mRNA to focal adhesions (Figure 2F,G, Figure 3—figure supplement 1B, Figure 3E–G and Video 7).
evidence: This is stated as a finding and supported by figures and video.

claim: Local confinement of ribosomes is mediated by mRNAs that are dwelling at specific local nanoenvironments at focal adhesions.
source: This indicates that local confinement of ribosomes is mediated by mRNAs that are dwelling at specific local nanoenvironments at focal adhesions.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the tethering experiment.

claim: β-actin confinement close to focal adhesions has previously been shown to be functionally important for global cell locomotion.
source: β-actin confinement close to focal adhesions has previously been shown to be functionally important for global cell locomotion (Katz et al., 2012), and our analysis now indicates that weak and local transient interactions mediate this confinement.

claim: Weak and local transient interactions mediate β-actin confinement close to focal adhesions.

claim: The MS2 labeling system was previously used to track movements of reporter RNA transfected into live cells, and demonstrated that reporter mRNAs moved through a variety of states in the cell cytoplasm, including corralled diffusion and directed motion.

The results corroborate and extend the hypothesis that actin translation in general is preferred around the focal adhesion complex.
